evals.prompt: is our fleet oversized, help me rightsize it
evals.expected_output: Pulls actual CPU, memory, disk, and network utilization over a window that includes peak traffic rather than guessing, and sizes to a high percentile (p95/p99) appropriate to the workload's failure mode instead of the average.

evals.prompt: we downsized an instance and now it's falling over during peak load
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses that sizing likely used average utilization or a quiet window instead of a peak-inclusive p95/p99 measurement, and recommends re-measuring after every resize to confirm the new size holds up under real traffic.

evals.prompt: let's just pick the smallest instance type that keeps CPU usage low
evals.expected_output: Pushes back that CPU and memory (and storage/IOPS where relevant) are separate sizing problems that must each be checked against their own utilization data, since a resource sized only on CPU can be undersized on another dimension.
